sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal
At the outset, learned counsel for the appellant prays for withdrawal of I.A.No.4703 of 2023, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A.No.4703 of 2023 is dismissed as withdrawn.
2. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, appeal is heard finally.

3. The appellant has filed present appeal under Section 374(2) of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:49873 2 CRA-3040-2023 Cr.P.C., being aggrieved of the judgment dated 17/01/2023, passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012) District Seoni (M.P.), in SC No.64/2021 arising out of the Crime No.27/2021 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Seoni.

4. It is submitted that as per prosecution story, the mother of the victim lodged a report on 28/09/2021 at Police Station Dundaseoni that she is resident of Jhuggi Basti Bordai, P.S.

sentences.text: She and her husband are working as labourers.
On 28/09/2021 at about 7:00 AM, she and her husband had gone to bypass chowk along with their cart which has been used to sell tea and snacks.
She had left all her four children in the house.

At about 2:00 PM, she came back to house,
prepared meals and then had given a tiffin to her eldest daughter for giving her husband at the shop.
She had consumed her food and was washing her clothes.

When younger daughter (prosecutrix)
came to her house, cried and stated that Shakil Chacha residing nearby had lured her with a Rs.10/-
note and said her to sit in his lap.

He had shown her a movie on his mobile phone and thereafter,
made her lay on a bed.
When he undressed her and had put fingers in her vagina.
Since, victim started feeling pain and was also had a sensation to pass a stool, she ran away from the house of Shakil chacha and came to the house of her mother and narrated her story.
5. On the basis of said version of the mother of the victim, FIR (Ex.P/1) was recorded.
Spot Map (Ex.P/2) was prepared and victim was subjected to medical examination.
Vide Ex.P/15 Shakil Khan was arrested.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed under Section NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49873 3 CRA-3040-2023 376(2)(J), 376AB of IPC and 3(b)/4 of POCSO Act, 2012.

6. After recording the evidence, the trial Court has convicted and sentenced the appellant as under :-
Conviction u/s Imprisonment (RI) Fine In lieu of 376(A)(B) IPC RI for 20 years Rs.3,000/- Additional RI for 06 months 7.
It is submitted that FIR (Ex.P/1) makes mention of the fact that the incident took place on 28/09/2021 at about 15:00 hrs.
Report was lodged at 20:01 hrs.
Thereafter, arrest memo of Shakil (Ex.P/15) is brought to the notice of this Court to show that Shakil was already taken into custody on 28/09/2021 at 11:30 hrs at Boredai.
It is submitted that when appellant was already in custody at 11:30 hrs then there was no occasion for him to have committed any wrong to the victim and therefore, the whole case has been concocted.

8. Reading from the DNA Finger Printing Unit Report (Ex.C/1), it is pointed out that on subjecting the samples obtained from 10 fingers of the appellant vis-a-vis the blood sample of the victim, the DNA profile was found to be negative.

9. It is further pointed out that mother of the victim (PW-1) has stated in para-5 of her cross-examination that she had gone to the Police Station along with one Rakesh Vishwakarma to lodge a report at about 3- 3:30 hr.
Report was immediately written which is contrary to Ex.P/1 wherein time of reporting FIR is mentioned as 20:01 hrs.

In para-1 she admitted that they had made a report to the government to dismantle the house of accused and, therefore his house was broken and since appellant was obstructing such NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49873 4 CRA-3040-2023 act, therefore police had taken him in custody.
Thus, it is evident that present is a case of false implication.

10. Reading from the evidence of Ms. Kailashpuri Dehariya, Sub- Inspector and Investigating Officer of the case, who is also present before the Court, in Para-13 admits that in Ex.P/9, on 28/09/2021 Shakeel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90157941/
2 makes a mention of 11:40 which means it was day time.

sentences.text: Ex . P/9
is the property seizure memo.
Now Ms. Kailashpuri Dehariya, Sub-Inspector submits that there was a mistake on her part in not writing AM and PM.
11 . Thus, plea of Ms. Kailashpuri Dehariya, Sub-Inspector is unfounded.
It is a case of faulty investigation.

When appellant was already in custody at 11:40 hrs as it admitted by PW-1 (mother of the victim) in her cross-examination that they had made a complaint against him for dismantling his house and since he was obstructing, he was taken into custody by police, there was no occasion for him to commit alleged offence at 3:00 PM.

Thus, when complete facts of the case are examined,
then it appears to be a case of false implication where role of the I.O. (PW-11) is suspected.

Para-13 of her cross-examination is quoted for ready reference :-
"13

It is unfortunate that the trial Court also became a party to such NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:49873 5 CRA-3040-2023 clever device of the prosecution and did not had ability to understand the evidence on record that when appellant was already in custody then there was no occasion for him to commit the alleged offence.
13. In view of such fact, we are of the opinion that present is a case of false accusation for the reasons best known to the prosecution.
Such device of the prosecution cannot be accepted.

Submission of Ms. Kailashpuri Dehariya, I.O. that she committed a mistake in not writing AM & PM can also not be accepted in view of the fact that in her cross-examination, she has admitted that 11:40 means 'day time 11:40' and she did not bother to clarify that appellant was arrested at 11:40 PM and not 11:40 AM.
Such gross negligence in discharge of duty by the Investigation Officer cannot be given a seal of approval.
Benefit of doubt needs to be accrued and is accrued in favour of the accused/appellant.
14. In the light of above observations, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment dated 17/01/2023 is set aside.
Appellant be released immediately, if not required in any other case.
15. State is directed to pay compensation of Rs.50,000/- (Fifty Thousand Only) for false accusation and taking away life and liberty of the appellant without there being any basis.
16. At this stage, Shri Nitin Gupta, learned Public Prosecutor submits that cost be reduced but this arguments needs to be rejected and is hereby rejected.

State on the one hand, claims itself to be champion and torch bearer of freedom of individual rights and on the other hand, its own officers in uniform, are violating the individual rights and they had no guts to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:49873 6 CRA-3040-2023 file a closure report after taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case.
